findings.title: TrustedRelease accepts arbitrary claimed ACCEPT, receipt hash, approval reference, Git commit, and Git tree without validating an independent hard-ACCEPT receipt or owner approval.
Current candidate preserves exact model-admission scoping and rejects discovery-only, expired, changed-policy, failed-native, and untrusted configuration paths.
Current candidate preserves revoke-CAS behavior: a late successful native verification cannot re-arm a concurrently revoked admission.

limitations: Independent recovery continued the original round-1 review and verified the exact 178-file manifest and aggregate candidate SHA-256; all 187 listed raw evidence hashes also matched their evidence manifest.

Independent dynamic checks: current Stable boundary suite passed 13 tests; current admission suite passed 30 tests. The independently authored fake Stable-approval metadata counterexample was accepted as Stable, including arbitrary non-Git commit/tree strings and no receipt or owner-approval object. That is an implementation defect, not merely a missing post-review deployment step.

The source currently treats review_receipt_sha256 and approval_ref as unverified shape fields. A corrective design must bind the approval record to an independently verifiable, immutable hard-ACCEPT reviewer receipt for the exact candidate/contract plus owner authorization, and validate the exact Git commit/tree values before Stable branding or execution; merely documenting those strings is insufficient.

The candidate's Stable test fixtures correctly describe themselves as synthetic and therefore do not provide a real Stable approval. Existing Chromium coverage establishes UI behavior for synthetic records only.

Raw evidence supports current real Codex and Claude native admissions and current real sequential, concurrent merge, loop, same-session recovery, lifecycle, and no-double-writer workflows. Physical backend and effective effort remain unknown where the supplied metadata says unknown.
The pre-review expiry rejection is preserved and appropriately did not start a stale-admission merge. It does not negate the later current successful native evidence, but it must remain retained.

The external fixed Gate, genuine PR delivery/readback, main merge, independently issued real approval, immutable Stable installation, launch/HTTP identity verification, and user UX acceptance are post-review conditions. They were not claimed performed here.

SP10 is blocked by the open SP01 provenance defect; after correction and a fresh independent review, external approval and deployment must be performed by the fixed external owner process, not candidate code.
